AMENDMENT NO. 2 SEPTEMBER 2008 TO IS 8431 : 1986 SPECIFICATION FOR TRACING PAPER
( First Revision ) (Page 6, clause 4.8, read with Amendment No. 1) -- Substitute 'Additional Requirements for ECO Mark' for 'Optional Requirements for ECO Mark'. (CHD 15)
Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, India

AMENDMENT NO. 1 SEPTEMBER 1993 TO IS 8431 : 1986 SPECIFICATION FOR TRACING PAPER
(First Revision) ( Page 3, clause 0.7 ) -- Add this new clause after clause 0.6 and renumber the subsequent clause: '0.7 A scheme for labelling environment friendly products known as ECO Mark has been introduced at the instance of the Ministry of Environment and Forests (MEF), Government of India. The ECO Mark would be administered by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) under the BIS Act, 1986 as per the Resolutions No. 71 dated 21 February 1991 and No. 425 dated 28 October 1992 published in the Gazette of the Government of India. For a product to be eligible for marking with ECO logo, it shall also carry the Mark of BIS besides meeting additional optional environment friendly requirements. For this purpose, the Standard Mark of BIS would be a single mark being a combination of the Mark and the ECO logo. Requirements to be satisfied for a product to qualify for the BIS Standard Mark for ECO friendliness, will be inlcuded in the relevant published Indian Standards through an amendment. These requirements will be optional; manufacturing units will be free to opt for the Mark alone also. This amendment is baaed on the Gazette Notification No. 455 dated 13 November 1992 for paper as environment friendly products published in the Gazette of India. This amendment is, therefore, being issued to this standard to include environment friendly requirements for tracing paper.' ( Page 6, clause 4.7 ) -- Add the following new clause after 4.7: '4.8 Optionl Requirements for ECO Mark 4.8.1 General Requirements 4.8.1.1 The product shall conform to the requirements for quality and performance prescribed under clauses 4.1 to 4.7. 4.8.1.2 The manufacturer shall produce to BIS, the environmental consent clearance from the concerned Stale Pollution Control Board as per the provisions of Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 and Air (Prevention and Control of Potation) Act, 1981 along with the authorisation, if required, under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and the rules made thereunder, while applying for ECO Mark.

1

4.8.2 Specific Requirements 4.8.2.1 The material shall be of the following two types depending on the raw material used in the manufacture: a) Type A -- Manufactured from pulp containing not less than 60 percent by mass of pulp made from materials other than bamboo, hard woods, soft woods and reed.

b) Type B -- Manufactured from pulp made from 100 percent waste paper.' ( Page 6, clause 5.1) -- Add the following new clause after 5.1: '5.1.1 For ECO Mark, the product shall be packed in such packages which shall be recyclable/reusable or biodegradable.' ( Page 7, clause 5.2.1 ) -- Add the following new clause after 5.2.1: '5.2.2 For ECO Mark, following additional information may also be marked on the container/package: The criteria for which the product has been labelled with ECO Mark.'

IS : 8431 - 1986

Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR TRACING PAPER

(First Revision)
0. F O R E W O R D
0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 27 February 1986, after the draft finalized by the Paper and its Products (Excluding Packaging Material) Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 Tracing papers are used in tracing of drawings, development of original drawings, base paper for sectional tracing papers and for other purposes. They may be natural ( untreated ) or treated (transparentized) with suitable materials. In addition to good transparency, tracing papers should have good strength and permanency so that they may be kept over long periods without deterioration or much change in opacity. 0.3 This specification was first published in 1977 based on tests carried out on indigenous samples at the Institute of Paper Technology, Saharanpur. 0.4 Of late, has been felt that there should be a clear cut distinction between tracing paper which have to be preserved for long and tracing paper which need not be preserved. In this revision, distinction is made between tracing paper of the permanent and non-permanent type. 0.5 The tracing paper covered in this standard is not meant for reproduction tracing purposes by contact printing and ammonia vapour development or moist development. Requirements of reproduction tracing paper is covered in IS : 9033-1978*. 0.6 This standard contains clauses 4.5, 4.6, 4.7 and 5.1 which call for agreement between the purchaser and the supplier and which permit the purchaser to use his option for selection to suit his requirements. 0.7 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, *Specification for reproduction tracing paper. 3

IS : 8431 - 1986 expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and methods of sampling and test for tracing papers used in tracing of drawings and development of original drawings. 1.2 This standard does not cover the requirements of diazo reproduction tracing paper. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in I S : 46611986 and the following shall apply. 2.1 Natural Tracing Paper, Permanent Type � Paper which has been made translucent by mechanical or similar means during the process of manufacture and rendered suitable for use with ink or pencil or both, meant for permanent records 2.2 Natural Tracing Paper, Non-Permanent Type -- Paper which has been made translucent by mechanical or similar means during the process of manufacture and rendered suitable for use with ink or pencil or both, not meant for longer preservation. 2.3 Treated Tracing Paper, Permanent Type -- Paper which has been treated with oil, resin, or waxes to make it translucent and suitable for use with ink or pencil or both, meant for permanent records. 2.4 Treated Tracing Paper, Non-Permanent Type -- Paper which has been treated with oil, resin, or waxes to make it translucent and suitable for use with ink or pencil or both, not meant for longer preservation. 3. TYPES 3.1 There shall be four types of tracing papers given below: a) Type 1 A -- Natural tracing paper, permanent type; b) Type 1 B -- Natural tracing paper, non-permanent type; c) Type 2 A -- Treated tracing paper, permanent type; and d) Type 2 B -- Treated tracing paper, non-permanent type. *Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised). Glossary of terms used in paper trade and industry (first revision) 4

IS : 8431 - 1986 4. REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Description -- All tracing papers shall be of uniform texture with smooth, matt or slightly grained surface and shall be free from spots, wrinkles, pinholes or other defects which may interfere with the intended use. The tracing paper shall be suitable for pencil and ink lines, yielding solid lines without skipping, feathering or spreading and shall not produce smudging. They shall not show surface cracks or abrasions in normal use to the extent that such cracks or abrasions are visible on prints made therefrom. 4.2 The paper shall also comply with the requirements given in Table 1 when tested in accordance with methods referred to in col 7 of the table.

*Methods of sampling and test for paper and allied products: Part 1 ( revised).

4.3 Accelerated Ageing -- Natural tracing paper permanent type ( Type 1A) and treated tracing paper, permanent type ( Type 2A ) shall be subjected to accelerated ageing by heating in an oven at 105 � 2�C for 72 hours, after which they shall be tested for folding endurance and opacity and shall satisfy the following conditions: a) The paper shall retain at least 50 percent of its original double fold; and b) The opacity shall not increase by more than 5 points for paper with nominal grammage up to 50 g/m2. Tn the case of higher nominal grammages, it shall not increase by more than 15 points. 5

IS : 8431 - 1986 The opacity of the aged specimen shall be determined for the same area as before ageing. 4.4 Drafting Tests 4.4.1 Lines shall be drawn upon different portions of the samples with a pencil containing black graphite 2H lead ( see IS : 1375-1981* ) and erased with eraser. There shall be no appreciable change in colour of the erased surface and no perceptible linting of the paper. For Types 1A and 1B tracing papers, the surface shall withstand at least three erasures and for Types 2A and 2B tracing papers, the surface shall withstand at least two erasures of lines drawn with pencil without leaving ghost or trace of sufficient intensity to produce an image on reprint. 4.4.2 Lines of varying widths of black drawing ink ( see IS : 7891971 ) shall be drawn upon different portions of the samples and carefully inspected. There shall be no appreciable spreading, feathering or skips. Both types of tracing papers shall withstand at least two erasures of ink lines drawn and redrawn. 4.5 Size and Tolerance on Sizes -- The tracing paper shall be in the form of either rolls or sheets as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. The sizes and tolerances on sizes shall be in accordance with IS : 1064-1980 or IS : 10711-1983� unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 4.6 Grammage and Tolerance on Grammage -- The grammage shall be as specified by the purchaser. A tolerance of �5 percent shall be allowed on the nominal grammage when tested in accordance with 6 of IS : 1060 (Part 1) - 1966||. 4.7 Optional Requirement -- If agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, Types 2A and 2B tracing paper shall also be suitable for printing charts and maps by means of multicolour off-set lithography and shall not develop any curl when so printed. 5. PACKING AND MARKING 5.1 The paper shall be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 5.2 Each package shall be marked with the following particulars: a) Description, type and grammage of paper; *Specification for black lead pencils (first revision ). Specification for ink, drawing, waterproof black (first revision). Specification for paper sizes (second revision). �Specification for sizes of drawing sheets. ||Methods of sampling and test for paper and allied products: Part 1 (revised). 6

IS : 8431 - 1986 b) Size of the paper; c) In the case of sheets the mass in kg per ream of 500 sheets including wrapping paper; in the case of rolls, the mass in kg of the roll including the mass of core and plugs; d) Lot number; e) Month and year of manufacture; and f) Manufacturer's name or recognized trade-mark, if any. 5.2.1 The containers may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 5.2.2 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

6. SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 6 1 Representative samples of packets or rolls of tracing paper shall be selected from each lot as prescribed in 3 of IS : 1060 ( Part 1 )-1966*. 6.2 Number of Tests -- Each of the packets or rolls selected from the lot shall be examined for size according to 5.5. From each of these packets or rolls, a test sample of the quantity sufficient to carry out all the tests given in the specification, shall be taken and examined for description given in 4.1. The test sample, having satisfied general requirements shall be tested for grammage, double fold, opacity, tear index, accelerated ageing and drafting. A test sample failing to meet any of these requirements shall be considered as detective.
NOTE -- For grammage, double fold, opacity and tear index, five test specimens shall be separately cut from each test sample and average of the five test results shall be repotted.

6.3 Criteria for Conformity -- A lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements of the specification, if the number of test samples found defective is less than or equal to the acceptance number. This acceptance number shall depend upon the size of the sample and shall be equal to zero if the sample size is less than 13. It shall be equal to 1 if the sample size is greater than or equal to 13.
*Methods of sampling and test for paper and allied products: Part 1 ( revised ). 7
